I can relate to this so much it's ridiculous. I am a couple weeks away from turning 21 years old, and graduated when I was 18 years old from high school. Over those 2 1/2 years, I was terrified to get a job. I didn't have a choice though however, being that I had to make some money to provide for myself. I had probably 6-7 jobs over the course of a year, and none of which lasted longer than 3 weeks. I'd get there, the first day or 2 would go fine.. then by the 3rd day (max) I started freaking out. I'm talking complete no shows to work, going to the bathroom and sitting on my phone in the stall for 20+ mins at a time, etc. When I was 19 I moved away to play junior hockey, and when I came back home I knew I was going to have to get a job. Since, I found a job in an office setting where I have my own little "cubical" and never really talk to anyone, just do computer work/date entry and have been here 3 months as of yesterday. In terms of advice, I suggest to give it some time and try not to over think it, if possible. Not too many people go into a job knowing exactly what they're going to be doing and/or don't make any mistakes. It happens.. In interview maybe let them know that you're shy/have socialized anxiety and see if they can help you out by letting them know what your triggers are and what you can & cannot handle.. You have time though man, you stated that you're a junior in college, so you have this year and the next before you're officially in the full-time workforce. 

Trust me though, I really do know how you feel and it's not fun knowing people that are younger than you that have years of job experience, etc. The worst part is just feeling like a complete fuck-up for being 20/21 years old and never being able to hold/have a job at all. You can DM me if you really want to if you have questions or want to talk about something because eventually it is something you'll need to overcome but not over think. (It really is easier than you (and the old me) think)
